sections.h2: Choosing how to sell in Issaquah
sections.html:
Two facts drive most decisions: how quickly you need the money and how much work the house needs. The median value of an owner-occupied home here is $963,000, so even a small swing in percentage terms is a big dollar difference. That makes a side-by-side comparison of routes worth the effort.

  • Traditional listing: the largest buyer pool and the longest runway. Budget time for prep work, showings, the buyer's inspection and financing conditions.
  • Selling without an agent: you take charge of pricing, photos, the purchase contract and the disclosure form.
  • Direct purchase for cash: no loan approval stands in the way of closing. Ask for price, closing date and your costs in a single written offer, then compare the net with your other options.

Issaquah sits about 15 miles east-southeast of Seattle at the south end of Lake Sammamish, along Interstate 90. Bellevue lies to the west and Sammamish to the north. Cougar, Squak and Tiger mountains frame the city, and much of that land is public park or forest. Sizable neighborhoods climb the lower slopes of Cougar and Squak, so slope and drainage are fair topics for a buyer to raise.

sections.h2: What you must tell a buyer
sections.html:
Washington's RCW 64.06.020 has the seller of improved residential property hand over a finished disclosure statement, unless the buyer gave up the right or the transfer is exempt. The deadline is five business days after both parties sign a written contract, unless they agree to something else. Afterward the buyer gets three business days to rescind.

The questions can be answered before you list. The title section covers authority to sell, first rights of refusal, options, leases and rental agreements, life estates, and encroachments or boundary disputes. Round up the deed, any lease, a survey and permit records ahead of time. A rushed form invites follow-up questions and delay.

sections.h2: Can a buyer add units on an Issaquah lot?
sections.html:
Possibly. Issaquah revised its code to meet state laws on middle housing and on accessory dwelling units, so ask the city what your lot allows. House Bill 1110 from 2023 directs cities to permit middle housing such as duplexes and townhouses in areas of mostly detached homes. House Bill 1337 directs them to allow at least two accessory dwelling units per lot beside the main home. The city's update also covered parking and street standards.

  • Permits: register at MyBuildingPermit.com to submit most permits.
  • Questions: Community Planning and Development answers at CPD@issaquahwa.gov or 425-837-3100, and offers online meetings with staff.
  • Larger projects: the city encourages a pre-application meeting.

Selling a house with a basement apartment, a detached unit or plans on file? Ask what permits exist, so the buyer does not inherit a surprise.

The seller usually covers the real estate excise tax, which goes to the county treasurer as of the sale date. Issaquah is in King County. The state portion steps up with price: 1.1 percent applies to the price up to $525,000, and 1.28 percent applies from there to $1,525,000. A local rate is layered on, and your escrow officer can calculate the total.

At a price near the city median, the amounts are large, so do not wait for closing day to learn them. Interest and penalties begin if the tax is unpaid a month after the sale. Ask escrow to show the figure on your closing statement before you sign. If you are also paying off a loan, the payoff and the tax both come out of the proceeds, so you will want the net figure in writing.

Interstate 90 and State Route 900 serve the city. Front Street through the historic downtown carries about 20,000 vehicle trips a day and is a chronic congestion point. The Issaquah Transit Center has 1,010 park-and-ride spaces and Issaquah Highlands has 819. Metro and Sound Transit Express buses run to Bellevue, Mercer Island, North Bend and Redmond, and a Link light rail line to Issaquah is proposed by 2050. Mean travel time to work is 25.3 minutes.

The Issaquah School District runs 28 schools for about 21,358 students, and its boundaries reach into southern Sammamish and northern Renton. Check the district for your exact address before you describe schools to a buyer. Mention the nearest park-and-ride too, because commuters to Bellevue, Mercer Island or Redmond will ask how far it is.

sections.h2: What to confirm before accepting an offer
sections.html:
• Read the offer for the closing date, the price and each cost assigned to you.
  • Order a payoff figure from your lender so the net amount is exact.
  • Ask the buyer how funds will be shown and whether any inspection or repair demand is attached.
  • Pull your permit history from Community Planning and Development, especially for a finished basement, a deck or a detached unit.
  • Have escrow estimate the state and local excise tax before you agree to a price.

Once you accept, expect the disclosure statement clock to start, escrow to open and the buyer's inspection to follow if the offer allows one. A cash buyer may skip the lender's appraisal, which usually shortens the stretch between acceptance and closing.

sections.h2: Pre-listing paperwork for an Issaquah house
sections.html:
A tidy folder pays off at any price point. Gather the deed, a survey if you have one, any lease or rental agreement, receipts for major work and the permit paperwork for anything you built or changed. Add your latest property tax statement and a payoff figure from each lender.

With those papers you can fill out the disclosure form accurately, answer a buyer's questions in one email and give escrow what it needs to prepare the settlement statement. If a document turns up missing, call Community Planning and Development at 425-837-3100 early, because records requests can take time.

faqs.q: Can I add a backyard cottage to my Issaquah property before selling?
faqs.a: Possibly. Under HB 1337 cities must allow at least two accessory dwelling units per lot, and Issaquah updated its code to match. Call Community Planning and Development at 425-837-3100 before you plan any building work.

faqs.q: How soon must I give the buyer a seller disclosure statement?
faqs.a: Within five business days after the written contract is accepted, unless the parties agree otherwise. The buyer then has three business days to rescind, and the statement may be waived or the transfer exempt.

faqs.q: Where do I apply for a building permit in Issaquah?
faqs.a: Register at MyBuildingPermit.com to submit most permits. For questions, contact Community Planning and Development at CPD@issaquahwa.gov or 425-837-3100, and ask about an online meeting or a pre-application meeting for larger projects.

The Issaquah School District, which runs 28 schools for roughly 21,358 students. Its boundaries include the southern part of Sammamish with zip code 98075 and the northern part of Renton, so check your exact address.

faqs.q: How far is Issaquah from Seattle, and how do I get there?
faqs.a: About 15 miles east-southeast of Seattle, along Interstate 90. Metro and Sound Transit Express buses connect Issaquah to Bellevue and Mercer Island, where riders can reach the Link 2 Line.
